To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a spike-element-wise (Spike-Element-wise) ResNet that is able to implement residual learning in deep spiking neural networks (SNNs).
we propose a novel spiking residual network that is capable of learning deep representations and is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance on various benchmarks.
we proposed a new residual block for SNNs and proved that it can overcome the vanishing and exploding gradient problems.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: (i) How to train deep SNSNs? (ii) What are the advantages and disadvantages of the SEW ResNets?  (iii) How to evaluate the SEW Resnets?  (iv) How to implement SEW ResNest on different platforms? (v) What is the potential of the SEW ReNest in real applications?
the problem of how to design deep SNNs for large-scale visual recognition.
the following questions: 1) Can we realize residual learning in SNNs? 2) Can we train deep SNN with more than 10 layers? 3) Can we train SNNs with fewer time-steps?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper proposes a novel architecture, spike-element-wise ResNet, for training deep SNN.
the SEW residual learning is an effective way to train deep SNI.
this work is an attempt to use Residual Networks for training deep Spiking Neural Networks, and that it is the first time to train SNNs with over 100 layers directly.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SEW Resnet can be used to train deep Snn in a very easy way, which can achieve better accuracy and more layers than other methods.
we propose the first successful deep residual learning in SNNs, and our SEW ResNets outperform the state-of-the-arts in both accuracy and efficiency.
the proposed SEW ResNet provides a simple way to train deep spiking neural networks with residual learning and can achieve higher performance in terms of accuracy and time-step.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SEW ResNets can easily implement identity mappings and overcome the degradation problem of Spiking ResNets.
the SEW block is a simple yet efficient way to implement residual learning in deep spiking neural networks.

SEW ResNets can be trained to achieve state-of-the-art performance on both image recognition and event-based vision tasks, and the proposed SEW ResNet provides a simple and effective method to train deep directly trained SNN models.
